item.title: Apple pushes Siri toward autonomous, cross-app actions
item.description: Apple’s new leadership is reportedly pressing Siri toward agentic actions across apps, signaling a strategic reset for its delayed AI ambitions.

item.title: ⚡ 12 quick hits — Evening edition, Nov 8
item.description: · Artificial Analysis launched decision-model benchmarks covering speed, cost, symmetry, and document-based judgment tasks.（X / Artificial Analysis） · Artificial Analysis reported that Celeris-1.1 Decision achieved the lowest task latency at 56 milliseconds in its decision-model comparison.（X / Artificial Analysis） · Artificial Analysis said decision-model prices ranged from $14 to $859 per million tasks, revealing a wide cost spread.（X / Artificial Analysis） · Simon Willison described implementing SQLite’s parse_number extension in both C and Rust, comparing portability and maintenance trade-offs.（Simon Willison） · Latent Space published a discussion of Stanford’s approach to teaching AI-native engineering with Mihail Eric and Monaco.（Latent Space） · GitHub said users can open a Copilot app session directly in VS Code and finish agent-started work inside their IDE.（X / GitHub） · Databricks made Document Intelligence REST APIs generally available for parsing, extraction, and classification in applications and agents.（X / Databricks） · Elvis and Eminem rights holders sued Suno, alleging its AI music system improperly clones protected voices and styles.（The Verge） · Recraft Studio added Flux 3 Video Max, Kling 4.0, and Bria Fibo 2 for video drafts, long scenes, and image generation.（X / Recraft） · InfoQ examined why AI video generation still creates costly rework despite faster models and increasingly capable creator tools.（InfoQ 中文） · Former Claude Code engineers discussed departures from leading AI laboratories and the pressures shaping frontier-team careers.（InfoQ 中文） · Tripo showcased Bluestone Lane, an interactive 3D story built with its API around cinematic environments and a small robot.（X / Tripo）

item.title: ⚡ 1 quick hits — Morning edition, Nov 8
item.description: · A U.S. AI-safety office lacks a permanent leader and has stopped publishing research, AP reports.（AP News）
